Warhammer 40k AI lab · 31 October 2026 · 11th edition rules

AI Critic Loop: rounds 1 to 5 and protocol v2

An LLM critic checks the decisions of the game AI. A rollout test measures each claim in victory points (VP). Each fix has an on/off parameter in the AI. Then paired games test each fix set against the shipped AI. From 31 October, protocol v2 adds stricter gates.

TLDR

Ask
Continue the AI critic loop. Ship the fixes that pass. Then apply the 6 rules of protocol v2 (V2-1 to V2-6). Report the results.
Issue
The shipped gains are small. Their 95% ranges include 0. Rounds 2, 3 and 5 shipped nothing. The bench fixtures use old army lists (40kdc-data 1.0.19). They have the current datasheet for 0 of 44 clear positions. Over two battle rounds, the re-check confirmed only 8 of 23 findings. The rules audit found 13 high-confidence places where the AI does not match the 11th edition engine.
Change
The lab shipped 1.56.7 (FIX_LONE_FLIP and FIX_REINFORCE_INSURANCE) and 1.56.8 (FIX_WAAAGH_ADVANCE_CHARGE). Against 1.56.6, they scored +0.80 [-1.00, +2.60] and +1.17 [-0.52, +2.86] VP per game, pooled. Round 5 shipped nothing. Thus the V2-6 stop rule ended the critic rounds at 08:57 UTC. Commit ca913e2 adds 13 audit fixes, all off. 11 of them passed the reach gate. Arm AUD plays these 11 fixes against 1.56.8. At look 1 (123 of 124 pairs), AUD scored +2.53 VP per game, pooled (z 2.36). This is below the ship boundary (3.710). Thus the arm continues to look 2. On the reserve fixtures, the screen_vs_objective fix failed the reach gate (0.17 lines per game). The lab parked it. The lab committed reserve fixtures (72a14a5), a tuning proposal (5b00fe0) and a fixture proposal (3ff20e3).

Summary

The critic loop ran rounds 1 to 5 on 30 and 31 October 2026. The AI now plays as version 1.56.8 (commit e12e6e8). This page gives the status after the AUD look-1 decision at 14:29 UTC on 31 October.

Versions 1.56.6 (round 1), 1.56.7 and 1.56.8 (both from round 4) came from the loop. Each gain is small. Against 1.56.6, version 1.56.7 scored +0.80 VP per game pooled [-1.00, +2.60]. Version 1.56.8 scored +1.17 [-0.52, +2.86]. Both ranges include 0.

At 02:59 UTC on 31 October, protocol v2 set stricter rules for new work. Under these rules, round 5 shipped nothing (gain 0 VP). Thus the stop rule (V2-6) ended the critic rounds at 08:57 UTC.

The 11th edition rules audit found 13 high-confidence AI-side mismatches. Commit ca913e2 adds a fix for each, all off. 11 fixes passed the reach gate. Arm AUD plays these 11 fixes against 1.56.8. At look 1, AUD scored +2.53 VP per game pooled (z 2.36, below 3.710). Thus it continues to look 2.

  • Shipped: 1.56.6 (f38e43a), 1.56.7 (1322dc2) and 1.56.8 (e12e6e8). See What shipped.
  • Not shipped: FIX_CHARGE_EV, FIX_FAR_TRIP, FIX_OVERCOMMIT, FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE, FIX_R1_HOME_CAPTURE and FIX_R1_SUPPORT_ADVANCE. Their code stays in the AI, with each parameter at 0. No round-5 design and no reserve-track design went into the AI.
  • Rounds 1 and 2: the rollout test measured 171 and 89 claims. 17 and 7 were clear. Round 1 shipped 1.56.6. Round 2 gave no gain.
  • Round 3: FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE changed no bench game (124 pairs, E 0.0). It is off.
  • Round 4: 185 rollout jobs, 20 clear. FIX_LONE_FLIP and FIX_REINFORCE_INSURANCE shipped as 1.56.7. FIX_WAAAGH_ADVANCE_CHARGE shipped as 1.56.8.
  • Round 5: 109 rollout jobs, 7 clear, 4 judge panels. No fix passed the gates. Shipped gain: 0 VP.
  • Re-checks over two battle rounds: 8 of 23 findings confirmed.
  • Rules audit: 75 items, 13 high-confidence fixes and 22 engine defects (listed, not fixed).
  • Reserve track: on the reserve fixtures, the screen_vs_objective fix printed 0.17 gate lines per game. The gate needs 1.0. The lab parked the fix.
  • Running: AUD look 2 (248 pairs).
  • For the owner: the tuning probe (recommendation: hold) and a new fixture with the current army lists. See Open decisions.

Open decisions for the owner

The lab does not start these items without a decision from the owner.

  1. Tuning probe. The V2-6 proposal recommends: hold. Do no tuning before the V2-2 decision on arm AUD. After that decision, run the one-generation probe one time at most. Estimated cost: 8.0 engineering hours and 22.5 to 49.1 container-hours. Simulated chance to ship a real gain: 0.10 at a 0.5 VP spread of true effects, 0.31 at 1.0 VP. See Tuning proposal.
  2. New fixture. The V2-5 proposal recommends: build asym_custodes_warhorde_2000_postdeploy first. It plays the current custodes_lions against the current Orks_2000. Use it as a separate extra gate. Do not pool it with the standard fixtures. Commit its pre-registration text before its first game. Estimated cost: 5.5 engineering hours or less, plus 1.0 to 1.6 container-hours to validate it.     • The 22 engine defects against the 11th edition rules (see Rules audit).

    • A change to V2-1 for fixes that act once per game.

Method

  1. Critic game. A sweep worker plays one AI-vs-AI game with the 11th edition rules. An LLM critic reads each important AI decision and its score breakdown. When the critic finds a worse choice, it writes a claim and one better action in a machine-readable form.
  2. Rollout test. The rollout tool loads the saved position. Branch A plays the AI choice. Branch B forces the critic action one time. Both branches play to the end of the next battle round (horizon 1) with 12 paired dice seeds. E is the mean of (B minus A) in VP margin for the deciding player. Under protocol v2, a re-check plays two battle rounds (horizon 2) with 24 seeds.
  3. Classify. Clear: the 95% range of E is wholly above 0. Promising: E is 1.5 VP or more and the range starts above -2.5. Harmful: the range is wholly below 0. Thus the AI choice was right. Not measured: the forced action did not apply, or all seeds gave the same result. From round 4, the page counts the second case as "no signal". A second run with 24 more seeds checks the best claims.
  4. Fix. One agent per cluster (a group of similar claims) finds the common cause in the decision records. It writes one general fix with a FIX_<KEY> parameter (0 = old behaviour). A unit test must fail on the old code and pass on the new code. A decision check replays the saved positions with the fix. From round 4, a judge panel selects the design: 3 designs, 2 reviews per design and 1 judge.
  5. Bundle test. Sibling cloud sessions play paired games with the 11th edition rules. In each pair, the candidate AI plays a base AI on one of three 2000-point fixtures. The two games of a pair swap the seats. E per pair = (M1 - M2) / 2, where M is the VP margin of player 2. Positive E means the candidate scores more. From round 3, a bench uses 124 seed pairs: 42 Custodes mirror, 42 asymmetric and 40 Orks mirror.
  6. Group test. Candidates with groups of fixes switched off play against the same base. The lab removes a fix that makes the result worse.
  7. Gates. Under protocol v2, a fix must act often enough on the bench fixtures before a bench (V2-1). The bench then runs in looks with a stop rule (V2-2). See Protocol v2.

Fixtures: mirror_custodes_2000_postdeploy (Custodes mirror), mirror_orks_2000_postdeploy (Orks mirror) and asym_2000_postdeploy (asymmetric). All three start after deployment. Reserve fixtures came later (see Reserve fixtures).

In rounds 1 and 2, one pair of games had a standard deviation of approximately 12 to 13 VP. Thus 40 pairs gave a 95% range of approximately plus or minus 4 VP. Four later code arms of 124 pairs had 9.6 to 11.3 VP per pair. Smaller effects need more games.

Terms

TermMeaning
EThe mean effect in VP. For a rollout: the mean of (B minus A) for the deciding player. For a bench: the mean of (M1 - M2) / 2 per pair. Positive E means that the candidate scores more.
95% rangeThe 95% confidence interval of E.
PooledThe mean over the three fixtures, with equal weight per fixture.
Clear, harmfulThe 95% range is wholly above 0 (clear) or wholly below 0 (harmful: the AI choice was right).
PromisingE is 1.5 VP or more, and the range starts above -2.5 VP.
No signalAll seeds gave the same result. Rounds 1 and 2 count these claims as not measured.
Horizon 1, horizon 2The rollout plays to the end of the next battle round (horizon 1) or of two battle rounds (horizon 2).
ConfirmedA re-check gives a 95% range wholly above 0. At horizon 2, the files call this CONFIRMED-H2.
Not confirmedA horizon-2 re-check does not meet the confirmed rule: its range includes 0, or the replay drifted. The table gives the reason (NOT CONFIRMED-H2).
FadedA re-check does not meet the confirmed rule, and the lab dropped the finding. At horizon 2, the files call this FADED-H2.
DriftThe replayed AI no longer makes the recorded choice. Thus the test measures a different decision.
GuardrailA measured position where the AI choice was right. A fix must not change it.
ClusterA group of similar claims. One fix design addresses one cluster.
ArmOne candidate AI setup that plays the base AI in a bench.
Pair, lookA pair is two games on one seed, with the seats swapped. A look is a planned decision point of the staged bench (V2-2).
ShardOne cloud session that plays a part of a bench or a re-check.
ReachLog lines per game that show a decision type, or a fix that changes a value (V2-1).
Datasheet matchThe current datasheet of the decision unit is on the fixture. The page writes: the bench has the current datasheet for N positions.
ParkedThe fix is not used. Its code stays, either in the AI with its FIX_ parameter at 0, or as a patch file in tools/ai_lab/.
zPooled E divided by its standard error (SE).
sNNNN rN, P1, P2A critic position: the game seed, the battle round and the player (player 1 or player 2).
CriticThe LLM that reads the AI decisions and writes claims. A review is a different step: it checks a fix design or its code.
Suggest (K) cardThe in-game card that shows the next action of the AI ("THE AI WOULD: ...").
Container-hourOne hour of one sibling cloud container.

Fixes

FIX_HELD_DUPShipped (on)
Claims8 (5 clear)
Best rollout+10.4 VP
Unit test14/14 (6 fail before)
Decision check2 of 8 match
Fix effect+1.5 VP [-0.3, +3.3]

Problem. The AI sent units, and reserve arrivals, to objectives that its army already held. The AI found control only within 3.79 inches of the marker. The 11th edition rules count every model on the terrain area that holds the objective. That area can extend approximately 6.7 inches from the marker. Thus the AI did not count its own units, or enemy units, on the far part of the ruin.

Change. The AI now counts the models on the terrain area of the objective when it finds control. Reserve units now arrive only at objectives where the plan needs more OC.

Proof. The unit test has 14 checks. 6 checks fail on the old code. All 14 pass with the fix. At the 8 saved positions, the AI now selects the critic option 2 times. At other saved positions, the unit also no longer goes to the held objective. The windowed scenario ai_held_objective_terrain_area shows the change in the game (21 of 21 steps pass). Group test: with this fix, the AI scored +2.1 VP per game more than without it (A minus C1). It also scored +3.1 VP more (D minus C2). The gain is largest in the Custodes mirror (+7.4 and +4.6 VP).

Decision check1 of 6 match
Fix effect-0.8 VP [-2.7, +1.2]

Problem. The AI sent fragile units alone to far objectives that the enemy held with more OC. The unit could not take the objective. The enemy killed it.

Change. A fragile unit does not go to a non-home objective when two conditions are true. First, the enemy OC there is more than the OC of the whole AI army there. Second, the enemy OC is at least two times the OC that the plan sends. A fragile unit has Toughness 3 or less, or 1 wound per model, or is a lone character.

Proof. The unit test has 8 checks. 4 checks fail on the old code. All 8 pass with the fix. At 1 of 6 saved positions, the AI now selects the critic option. Group test: its own effect is uncertain. Alone against V6, it scored -1.5 VP per game. In V7, the AI with this fix off scored 2.4 VP less. It stays on because the lab tested the shipped set (D) as a whole.

FIX_CHARGE_EVDropped (off)
Claims2 (1 clear)
Best rollout+9.0 VP
Unit test11/11 (5 fail before)
Decision check1 of 2 match
Fix effect-0.8 VP [-2.5, +1.0]

Problem. When several units charged one target, the AI added a kill bonus for each declared charger. It also counted chargers with a failed charge. Thus the AI made poor charges after a failed charge.

Change. The AI now counts only chargers that arrived. When the damage from the units that arrived already kills the target, the AI adds no kill bonus.

Proof. The unit test has 11 checks. 5 checks fail on the old code. All 11 pass with the fix. At 1 of 2 saved positions, the AI now selects the critic option. The other claim faded with 24 more seeds. Group test: the set without this fix (D) scored +1.6 VP per game against V6. The set with it (A) scored +1.0 VP. The switch-off test also showed the AI better with it off (+2.2 VP). It is off by default. The code stays in the AI.

Fixes

FIX_FAR_TRIPDropped (off)
Claims5 (2 clear after 36 seeds)
Best rollout+2.8 VP (36 seeds)
Unit test11/11 (fails before)
Decision check3 of 5 match
Bundle (with OC)Custodes -6.3 VP

Problem. The AI sent a durable unit alone on a trip of 2 or more turns to an objective. There, the enemy would have more OC. Three parts of the movement plan sent a unit to the next objective that needed OC. They did this also when the unit had a poor chance there. These parts are pass 2, the quicker-unit swap and the backfill. The race penalty only halved the score. FIX_LONE_TRIP covered only fragile units.

Change. The AI skips a capture trip of 2 or more turns by any unit when two conditions are true. First, the help that can join brings less OC than the unit. Second, the enemy OC there is more than the OC of the holders, the unit and the help together. The unit then supports an objective where it can help.

Proof. The unit test has 11 checks. It fails on the old code and passes with the fix. At 3 of 5 saved positions, the AI now selects the critic option, with both fixes merged. Related AI tests pass.

FIX_OVERCOMMITDropped (off)
Claims1 (clear)
Rollout+4.4 VP [2.1, 6.6] (36 seeds)
Unit test8/8 (fails before)
Decision check1 of 1 match
Re-test (alone)Custodes -1.6 VP (n20)

Problem. The AI sent a second unit on a 2-turn trip to an objective where another unit already went. The AI lost the race even with both units (approximately 18 OC against approximately 30 enemy OC). Another objective that needed OC was available.

Change. A top-up unit with a trip of 2 or more turns does not join a race that it cannot win. The test: the plan loses the race also with that unit. Then the unit goes to its best other objective that still needs OC. It must get there no later than to the first objective. When there is no such objective, the top-up stays.

Proof. The unit test has 8 checks. It fails on the old code and passes with the fix. At the saved position, Custodian Guard Beta now goes to obj_nml_2. The windowed scenario ai_overcommit_lost_topup shows the change in the game (21 of 21 steps pass).

Decision. The lab set the rule before the round-2 data. It keeps the fixes if two conditions are true. The pooled E against V7D is above 0. No fixture 95% range is wholly below 0. Round 3

Round 2 left three clear claims at position s7437 without a fix. Round 3 tested the claim at battle round 1. There, the AI kept the only holder of its home objective in place, but nothing threatened that objective. Over 36 seeds, the critic option scored +7.31 VP [+4.98, +9.63].

FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE (candidate V9, commit 5e70bc2) lets that holder leave when all of these conditions are true:

  • The primary card pays nothing for the home objective.
  • No enemy unit can get to the home objective before the end of the enemy's next turn.
  • Another unit can step back onto the home objective in one move.
  • The holder is not fragile.

The bench played V9 against V7D in 124 pairs with the 11th edition rules. There were 42 Custodes mirror pairs, 42 asymmetric pairs and 40 Orks mirror pairs. In every pair, both games gave the same margin. Thus the pooled E was 0.0. The bench showed no effect from the fix. The rule needs a pooled E above 0. FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE is off (commit 14eb69f). The code stays in the AI.

The reinforce claim at s7437, battle round 2, went into round 4 (cluster reinforce_insurance). The 8% charge claim at s7437, battle round 2, player 2, did not stay clear. Over 36 seeds, it measured +1.50 VP [-0.67, +3.67].

Sources: commits 5e70bc2 and 14eb69f, STATUS.md (decisions), tools/ai_lab/r4_designs/measured_positions.json (the s7437 values, raw E 7.305 and 1.5) and fix_args_r4.json (charge_low_odds hint: the round-3 low-odds charge finding faded with more seeds).

Problem. A friendly unit near an objective that the enemy controls made the AI read that objective as taken. Thus the AI sent its next unit alone to flip another objective that the enemy held with more OC. At s7454, battle round 3, the AI sent Custodian Guard Gamma alone to obj_nml_1, where the enemy had OC 14. The critic option, an Advance to obj_center, scored +21.50 VP [+16.93, +26.07].

Change. The AI no longer reads an enemy-controlled objective as taken when a friendly unit stays on it.

Proof. The windowed scenario ai_lone_flip_s7454 passes 25 of 25 steps. With the fix, the Suggest (K) card sends Gamma to obj_home_2. It sends Alpha to flip obj_center, and Beta holds it. The scenario does not execute the plan. The arm with only this fix (LF-only) scored +0.79 VP per game pooled against V7D [+0.03, +1.55]. Its range is wholly above 0.

Problem. The AI sent units to reinforce objectives that it already held. At s7437, battle round 2, Custodian Guard Beta reinforced obj_center. The AI already held obj_center with OC 6. The critic option, an Advance to obj_nml_2, scored +4.36 VP [+0.61, +8.12].

Change. The fix has three parts, each with its own switch. RI_RACE: the AI no longer gives full value to the reinforcement of a held objective in one case. In that case, the enemy can bring 1.5 times or more of the OC that the AI would have there. That OC includes this unit. The reinforcement then keeps only half of its objective value. The check measures the enemy move range from the nearest model of each unit. RI_QUARTER: with the Reconnaissance Sweep mission, the AI counts the VP of an uncovered table quarter. RI_ASSAULT: a unit whose ranged weapons all have [ASSAULT] Advances on long trips.

Proof. The windowed scenario ai_reinforce_insurance_s7437 passes 25 of 25 steps. With the fix, Beta advances toward obj_nml_2. The centre reinforcement gets the RI_RACE penalty: the enemy can bring approximately 42 OC, against 17 OC for the AI. Alone (RI-only), this fix scored -0.21 VP per game pooled. With FIX_LONE_FLIP on, it added +0.22.

Problem. The AI read the Waaagh! rule text as if Ork units could charge after an Advance in every turn. Thus Ork melee units Advanced "to attack" and lost the charge. At s7468, battle round 3, Stormboyz Advanced toward Prosecutor Squad and could not charge. The critic option, a Normal move to obj_nml_1, scored +6.14 VP [+3.08, +9.19].

Change. A unit without an advance-and-charge effect makes a Normal move toward its charge target. It keeps the charge. While a Waaagh! or another advance-and-charge effect is active, the unit still Advances. During such an effect, the Advance does not stop the charge. The fix keeps the attack. Thus it matches the critic option only in part.

Proof. The unit test has 10 checks. All 10 pass. 14 other AI test suites pass. The windowed scenario ai_waaagh_advance_charge_s7468 passes 27 of 27 steps (screenshots below). V12 C_waaagh scored +1.17 VP per game pooled against V7D.

Bench on (V12 C_full)-0.05 VP [-2.03, +1.93]

Problem. In battle round 1, the AI sent a unit in support on a long trip to a contested objective. The unit made a Normal move, but an Advance arrives a turn sooner. At s7451, battle round 1, player 2, Custodian Guard Gamma made a Normal move toward obj_center. The critic option, an Advance, scored +5.86 VP [+3.09, +8.63] over 36 seeds.

Change. The winning design ("game") gives each part its own switch. FIX_R1_SUPPORT_ADVANCE makes the support unit Advance in this case. FIX_R1_HOME_CAPTURE covers the home capture at s7468, battle round 1 (+6.86 VP [+4.45, +9.27]). There, Custodian Guard Gamma moved toward obj_home_1, and Alpha also went there. FIX_R1_HOME_CAPTURE fires 0 times on the bench fixtures, because every home objective has a holder at deployment. Thus the lab parked it at 0 in V11, V12 and 1.56.8. FIX_R1_SUPPORT_ADVANCE is on in V12 C_full and off in V12 C_waaagh.

Proof. V12 C_full scored -0.05 VP per game pooled and failed the rule. V12 C_waaagh scored +1.17. Thus FIX_R1_SUPPORT_ADVANCE is off in 1.56.8. The code of both switches stays in the AI.

Decisions, with rules set before the data

  • V10. V10 met the rule (+0.80) and shipped as 1.56.7 (commit 1322dc2, 23:41 UTC on 30 October).
  • Group test (rule set at 23:12 UTC). Keep the arm among V10, LF-only and RI-only with the highest pooled E that meets the rule. V10 (+0.80) stays. LF-only (+0.79) is second. RI-only fails the rule. Thus switch_lf_only.sh did not run.
  • What the switch-off arms show. LF-only has almost the same E as V10 and a narrower range. Many of its pairs gave the same result: Custodes 19, asymmetric 34, Orks 29. RI alone adds nothing. With FIX_LONE_FLIP on, it adds +0.22 (interaction).
  • V12 (rule set at 00:52 UTC). Pick the V12 arm with the highest pooled E. It ships only if it meets the rule and beats V10 (+0.80) on the same seeds. At 03:57 UTC, V12 C_waaagh (+1.17) met both conditions. It shipped as 1.56.8 (commit e12e6e8, 04:14 UTC).
  • Note. The pooled range of V12 C_waaagh includes 0 (z approximately 1.36). Under protocol v2 (V2-2), it would not pass look 1 (z 3.710). It shipped because the lab set its rule under v1. Work that started before v2 finished under its own rules.

The review before the 1.56.8 release found two older defects. 1.56.8 did not cause them. First, tests/test_ai_objective_assignment_fixes.gd has 6 passes and 1 failure, also on V10. It is not in tests/ci/direct_known_failures.txt. Second, IngressMove sets flags.no_moves_until_charge_phase, and nothing clears it. Thus MovementController hides Move and Advance for units that arrived from reserves, in every later turn. This affects the human UI only. MovementPhase does not apply the flag. Thus the flag does not affect the AI.

Protocol v2

The lab wrote protocol v2 at approximately 02:58 UTC on 31 October, before it had any v2 data. Commit 27fac2c (02:59:43 UTC) records that order. The file is tools/ai_lab/protocol_v2.md.

Work that started before v2 finished under the v1 rules:

  • the V12 bench and its 00:52 rule
  • the 4 round-5 judge panels
  • the round-5 sweeps r5c06, r5c07, r5c08 and r5c10

All other work follows v2.

Context

The protocol file does not give its reason in words. The lab records showed these facts before 02:59 UTC:

  • A bench can show no effect from a fix. In round 3, all 124 pairs were identical (E 0.0). Round 4 parked screen_vs_objective because the bench gives identical pairs.
  • The benches had low power. The 124-pair benches had a pooled standard error (SE) of 0.39 to 0.92 VP. Of the arms complete before 02:59 UTC, only LF-only had a pooled 95% range wholly above 0.
  • One-round rollouts can mislead. In the pr10 re-check with 24 seeds, 2 of 11 findings faded. In round 2, fixes that passed every gate still lost 6.26 VP per game in the Custodes mirror.
  • The round-4 charge_low_odds panel (commit f9dbb8e, 20:55 UTC on 30 October) found a rules gap. The AI applies a 10th edition overwatch cost at charge time (T7-51). The 11th edition engine does not apply this cost.
  • The bench fixtures have no units in reserve at the start (84 of 84 deployed).
  • The shipped gains were small. Round 2 gave none, and round 3 gave 0.0. Round 4 gave +0.80 VP, with a range that includes 0.

Later, at 03:19 UTC, the charge study (commit 7736b71) also found that the bench fixtures have no attached leaders.

The 6 rules

RuleWhat it requiresResult so far
V2-1 Bench-reach gateThe decision type of a cluster must print at least 1.0 log line per game before design. The log tag of each fix must do the same before a bench. The cluster gate counts 6 distinct games (2 pairs per fixture, the shipped AI in both seats). The fix gate uses 1 pair per fixture (6 games). Below 1.0, park the fix: keep the code, and keep its FIX_ parameter at 0.Round 5: all 4 clusters passed at the decision-type level. The charge_target fix failed the fix gate (0.33). Audit bundle: 11 of 13 fixes passed. Reserve track: the screen_vs_objective fix failed (0.17).
V2-2 Sequential benchEach new arm plays the shipped AI. Looks come at 124, 248 and 372 pairs. Ship only if z is at least 3.710, 2.512 or 1.993 at that look (Lan-DeMets O'Brien-Fleming, one-sided alpha 0.025). Also, the 95% range of each fixture must not be wholly below 0. A non-binding futility stop applies when pooled E is 0 or less at look 1 or 2.Arm AUD look 1: continue (pooled E +2.53, z 2.36, below 3.710). Look 2 runs now.
V2-3 Longer value checkBefore a finding enters a panel, re-check it over two battle rounds. If the decision is in round 4 or 5, re-check it to the game end. Use 24 seeds and seed base 5300. Keep the finding only if the 95% range is wholly above 0 (CONFIRMED-H2). Otherwise, drop it (the protocol calls this FADED).8 of 23 findings confirmed.
V2-4 11th edition rules auditList every rule assumption in AIDecisionMaker.gd. Compare it with the engine and the 11th edition core rules. Make a second agent try to disprove each mismatch. Then rank the mismatch. Give each high-confidence AI-side fix a FIX_ parameter (0 = old behaviour) and a failing-first test. Put all of them in one bundle arm. List engine defects. Do not fix them in this track.75 items, 13 high-confidence fixes, 22 engine defects.
V2-5 Broader benchReserve fixtures become an extra gate for reserve-dependent fixes. First, they need a "usable" review, a fixture_check pass and smoke games without errors. Propose one more faction fixture. Do not run it.Reserve fixtures usable (72a14a5). The screen_vs_objective fix failed the gate on them (0.17). Fixture proposal ready (3ff20e3).
V2-6 Stop ruleThe round-5 gain is the pooled E of the round-5 bundle that ships under V2-2, or 0 if none ships. If it is +0.5 VP or less, run no new critic sweeps or rounds. Propose a tuning track with cost and time. Do not run it.Triggered at 08:57 UTC (gain 0 VP). Proposal: hold.

The lab simulated the power of V2-2 with the futility rule:

Chance to ship16%49%78%88%

This is approximately 80% power for true gains of approximately 0.7 to 1.5 VP.

The decision tool .ai_lab_work/decide_v2.py computes the looks, z, the fixture check and the futility stop. The lab wrote it at 03:26 UTC and tested it on V12 C_full data (a tooling test only).

The standing rules do not change. Make no pull requests. Push only to claude/awesome-clarke-31p54m. Never claim a result that did not run. Never remove debug logs. Wait for a condition, not for a fixed time. Archive each sibling session after you read its result.

Problem. At s7480, battle round 3, Allarus Custodians declared one charge at two Allarus units. The AI picked the target after the roll. The critic option, a charge at a third unit, Blade Champion Alpha (4.3" away), scored +5.75 VP over 24 seeds.

11th edition rules audit

The V2-4 audit compared each rule assumption in AIDecisionMaker.gd with the game engine and the 11th edition core rules. A workflow of 13 agents did the work: 6 topic auditors, 6 verifiers and 1 ranker. Each verifier tried to disprove the items of one topic. The workflow played no games. The rules text came from a snapshot of the wahapedia 11th edition core rules (267 KB). Commit 585cbbc (06:18 UTC) holds the result.

75items
71confirmed
4refuted
13high-confidence fixes

Items per topic: charges 13, movement and keywords 11, army rules 10, reserves 13, objectives 13 and stratagems 15. The ranker kept 51 entries. In 46, the AI does not match the engine. In 5, the AI does not match the rules. The audit lists 22 engine defects against the rules separately. This track does not fix them.

A high-confidence fix (rank CLEAR in rules_audit_11e.md) compares the AI with the engine. It acts on the 3 standard fixtures. It is a small change with a new FIX_ parameter and a failing-first test. Line numbers refer to HEAD 856d61b. AIDecisionMaker.gd has 27577 lines and did not change after e12e6e8.

The 13 high-confidence fixes

RankFixAudit IDMismatchEstimate
not measured
1FIX_OBJ_AREA_REACHOC-01Move-range and contest checks measure from the unit centre to the objective marker (3.79"). But every bench objective is a terrain area. One model on any part of it can control it. This is the largest systematic mismatch.+0.5 to +2 VP per game
2FIX_CHARGE_OW_11ECH-01, OW-01Every charge score includes a 10th edition Fire Overwatch penalty at charge time (T7-51). The 11th edition engine never resolves it. Its main source, the Stompa, is TITANIC and cannot fire overwatch.More charges. Sign not known.
3FIX_OBJ_AREA_ON_OBJOC-03Target value reads "on objective" as a unit centre within 3.79" of the marker. On bench terrain objectives, this misreads 63% of the real holders.+0.3 to +1 VP per game
4FIX_OBJ_AREA_HOLDOC-04The hold, charge-off, fall-back and chase checks use the marker distance and OC sums without the terrain area.+0.2 to +1 VP per game
5FIX_EOG_TIMINGOC-02The AI values end-of-battle primary awards as if they paid at the next scoring point in every round. This affects approximately 48% of bench games.Approximately 0.3 to 0.7 VP pooled
6FIX_MOVE_TERRAIN_11ETER-01Normal moves and Advances of non-INFANTRY units use the charge terrain cost. Every terrain piece blocks them. The engine adds 2" for difficult ground, plus the climb. Only dense features over 2" block a move.Small to moderate (Ork seats only)
7FIX_HI_CHARGE_ODDSCH-03, HI-01The AI values Heroic Intervention without the 2D6 charge roll. In full standard games, 9 of 16 Heroic Interventions failed.+0.2 to +0.6 VP

10FIX_PILEIN_TARGETS_11ECH-09Pile-in and consolidation use the 10th edition "closest enemy model of any unit". The engine measures to the pile-in targets only and rejects the move. In one measured game, it rejected 5 pile-in and 6 consolidation moves.Small
11FIX_CHARGE_REROLL_ODDSCH-05, AR-03Blade Champion charge odds ignore the free Swift Onslaught re-roll. With a 9 needed, the odds go from 0.28 to 0.48.Sign not known

14FIX_WAAAGH_ADV_REROLLAR-06Ork and Blade Champion Advance odds assume a plain D6. The engine gives a free re-roll, and the AI takes it on 1 to 3. P(D6 of 3 or more) goes from 0.67 to 0.83.Probably below 0.3 VP per game

Rank 13 is RS-01 (From Golden Light timing). It is not a high-confidence fix.

OC-01, OC-03 and OC-04 concern the gap that round 1 found. FIX_HELD_DUP (1.56.6) made the control check use the terrain area. The move-range, target-value and hold checks still measure to the marker.

Refuted items and engine defects

The audit refuted 4 items:

  • CH-08: the +2" term is not an over-estimate.
  • ADV-02: 1.56.8 already has this fix.
  • Movement CH-01: the gang-up seed never runs on the bench.
  • OC-11: round-1 positions do score. This is a tuning question.
Show the 22 engine defects against the 11th edition rules (report only)
  • CH-13, HI-04 and HI-03: Heroic Intervention has no Fights First. It picks the target before the roll. Into the Fray costs 1 CP, not 2.
  • CO-02: Counteroffensive marks the unit as fought, not as selected. Thus the same player selects again.
  • HI-02 (root part): the Heroic Intervention check rejects every VEHICLE without WALKER (10th edition wording).
  • CR-01 (engine part): the engine offers Command Re-roll on battle-shock tests. Also, it re-rolls both dice.
  • GR-01: a unit that uses Explosives counts as a unit that shot. The stratagem check looks only for GRENADES.
  • CI-01: the engine uses the 10th edition Tank Shock, not Crushing Impact (rule 15.06).
  • SM-01: the engine offers Smokescreen after the attacker selects targets, and only for the target unit (rule 15.10).
  • Reactive window: the engine opens the reactive shooting-stratagem window only for a human defender.
  • TER-02: the engine adds 2" per difficult-ground piece to the Normal moves and Advances of non-INFANTRY units. Rule 13.06 has no such cost.
  • CQ-01: an engaged unit can shoot only with a PISTOL weapon, or as a MONSTER or VEHICLE. The engine does not read the 11th edition close-quarters tags.
  • FLY: the engine has no take-to-the-skies option. FLY units move through enemy models without it (rule 21.03).
  • RS-02: the engine locks a unit that arrived from reserves for the whole battle round. Rule 20.04 locks it only until the next Charge phase (Custodes mirror: 121 of 224 games).
  • RS-04: bench Allarus have the 10th edition From Golden Light. The engine tests it at 1", not 2".
  • Reserves: destroyed reserve units stay IN_RESERVES. Rapid Ingress spends its CP before the engine checks the placement.
  • RS-11: the engine adds a 50% unit-count cap for reserves. It also measures the points cap against the actual army points (rule 20.01).
  • RS-13: the engine accepts an ingress set-up before the coherency test (rule 03.02).
  • OC-08: the engine finds objective control at the start of the Command phase. It then scores from that state, also after Battle-shock changed the OC.
  • OC-12: the engine updates objective control after every move or charge. Rule 14.02.01 changes control only at the end of a phase or turn.
  • Burden of Trust: the engine measures "within range" from the base edge to the marker (3" plus 20 mm). Rules 14.01 and 14.02 use the terrain area.
  • Consolidation: the engine requires engagement with every enemy unit within 3", not with one or more selected units (rule 12.08).
  • IB-01 (engine part): the engine tests the battle-shock of an Attached unit against the highest Ld in the unit.
  • AR-02: the bench saves use old 40kdc-data 1.0.19 data.

Bench and harness facts from the audit

This track does not fix these items. The audit flags them to the owner.

  1. From Golden Light seat. The AI of P1 decides END_TURN_REDEPLOY (From Golden Light) for the unit of P2 (AIPlayer.gd:2252). All 224 of 224 records log player 1. Also, the function evaluate_rapid_ingress never sets _current_player. Thus profile arms read the parameters of the opponent. In an A/B arm, any From Golden Light fix shows the wrong sign. This stays true until the decision moves to the seat of the owner.
  2. Bench rosters. The bench uses 40kdc-data 1.0.19 Kult of Speed Orks and older Custodes datasheets with Blade Champions that are not attached. War Horde, Lootas, [HEAVY] and close-quarters items have 0 bench reach.
  3. Reserves. The standard Custodes bench is not free of reserves after round 1. From Golden Light and On Gilded Wings put Allarus into reserves, approximately 4 placements per game in the Custodes mirror.
  4. Aggression. Bench Custodes faction aggression resolves to 1.0. The AI never uses FACTION_AGGRESSION_CUSTODES (1.5). SEED-REAL never runs on any seat.
  5. Reactive window. AI defenders never get the reactive shooting-stratagem window: ShootingPhase.gd:2932-2933 opens it only for a human defender. 5 to 21 offers per game get no answer. Thus the bench cannot measure fixes for defensive stratagems.
  6. Follow-ups. The AI ignores Custodian Guard abilities: Praesidium Shield (approximately 22 fires per game) and Stand Vigil (approximately 36 per game). The bench cannot A/B test some engine-side AI policies: Salvus 18" and the constant FURY score.

Sources: tools/ai_lab/rules_audit_11e.md (lines 9-15, 75-216 and 218-248) and rules_audit_11e.json (commit 585cbbc), STATUS.md.

Audit bundle and its bench

Workflow wf_194da67a-997 built the 13 high-confidence fixes in 5 groups. The groups are G_OBJ (3), G_MISC (3), G_CHG (3), G_FIGHT (2) and G_ADV (2). Each group had a review that tried to disprove its fixes and re-ran the failing-first tests. A repair step and a merge followed (bundle.patch, 11:33 UTC). The fixes must change only AIDecisionMaker.gd, because the bench swaps only that file. The workflow used 12 agents. A container restart between 09:00 and 09:09 UTC stopped it. It resumed from its cache.

11pass the gate

Each new parameter at 0.0 gives the shipped 1.56.8 behaviour.

Reviews and the repair

The reviews approved 12 fixes and confirmed that each test fails first. FIX_MOVE_TERRAIN_11E got "needs_changes" because it also changed the AI of the other seat. AIPlayer.gd:1699 (a recompute after an Advance roll) and :2788 (a staging retry) call AIDecisionMaker._compute_movement_toward_target directly for both seats. Thus the fix in the profile of the candidate also acted on the units of the base seat.

The repair adds the gate _move_terrain_fix_on(unit). It is true only when the parameter is on and the owner of the unit is the current player. All 10 places in the code that check the fix use this gate. 2 new seat tests fail on the AI before the repair (21 pass, 2 fail). The lab probed 361 decisions with the fix on only in the profile of the opponent. Before the repair, the AI changed 175 of them. The repaired AI changed 0.

A replay of the game with this fault (Orks mirror, seed 91201) shows the same result. The repaired AI printed 161 tags, all in the phases of P2. Before the repair, it printed 220 tags, and 38 of them were in the movement of P1. The lab did not make the harness fix: route both calls through _dm(player). This fix needs a change to the shared AIPlayer.gd.

Tests and the identity check

With all 13 new parameters at 0.0, 23 of 23 test files pass. These are 13 new files and 10 existing fix tests.

With all 13 fixes on, 17 of 23 files pass. In 6 files, some checks fail, because each test switches on only its own fix. Failed checks per file: far_trip 4, held_dup 1, lone_flip 1, keeper_release 1, r1_home_capture 8 and waaagh_adv_reroll 2. Update these checks before you ship the fixes. The lab did not run them with only the 11 AUD fixes on.

Reserve fixtures and the screen track

Commit 72a14a5 (04:22 UTC) adds 3 reserve fixtures. The smoke test and the review both said "usable".

The builder 40k/tests/make_2000pt_fixture.gd has two new opt-in flags. The flag --reserves=ai runs the real FormationsPhase with the AI for both seats. It puts the units that the AI picks for reserve into reserve. The flag --base=<fixture> selects the base fixture. Without the flags, the builder does not change: decoded saves and .meta are identical on 4 configs.

FixtureIn reserve, per sideShare

mirror_orks_2000_reserves_postdeployStormboyz C and D (Strategic Reserves), Deffkoptas A and B (Deep Strike).410 of 1975 pts, 4 of 17 units

The fixture_check tool passes these fixtures only without --strict. 7 full smoke games had 0 SCRIPT ERRORs. All Custodes reserves arrive in round 2. The [SCREEN] deep-strike logic fires 3 to 6 times per game, against 0 to 1 on the standard fixtures.

Role: an extra gate for reserve-dependent fixes. The 3 standard fixtures stay the ship gate. Prefer the Custodes and asymmetric reserve fixtures. The AI often fails to place its Deffkoptas (defect 3 below). The Orks mirror fixture has them in both seats. The asymmetric fixture has them in one seat.

Defects found (not fixed)

  1. Engine: destroyed reserve units keep IN_RESERVES (ScoringPhase P1-37). Thus destroyed units can arrive again in round 4. Also, Rapid Ingress on a destroyed unit costs CP.
  2. A Rapid Ingress whose placement fails still costs 1 CP. There is no refund.
  3. AI: the engine rejects the Deep Strike and Rapid Ingress placements of the AI for the oval-base Deffkoptas. The cause is walls. The function _is_valid_reinforcement_position has no per-model wall or oval check. The engine destroys those units at the end of round 3.
  4. AI: the movement-order comparator is not a strict weak ordering ("bad comparison function").
  5. Bench logs contain MCP-bridge noise, because run_lanes does not set GODOT_MCP_DISABLED=1.
  6. The datasheets of the bench fixtures are older than the current army lists (an older defect).

Correction from the rules audit: the standard Custodes mirror is not free of reserves after round 1. From Golden Light and On Gilded Wings put Allarus into reserves, approximately 4 placements per game.

screen_vs_objective reserve track. The finalizer committed the final code at 13:56 UTC (commit 233bdd2: final.patch and final.json). The code is not in AIDecisionMaker.gd.

  • Decision checks: the fix changes 1 of 5 measured findings. At s7467, the Gretchin now Advances toward obj_nml_2, as the critic asked.
  • The other 4 findings (s7465, s7484, s7482 and s7481) send a unit to obj_center. There, the enemy holds the objective, contests it next move or wins the race. The judge change RC3 excludes this case.
  • Guardrails: the lab replayed 45 measured positions with the final code. The fix fired at 2 of them and at no harmful position.
  • V2-1 gate on the 3 reserve fixtures: 0.17 [SCREEN_VS_OBJECTIVE] lines per game, pooled (Custodes 0.0, asymmetric 0.5, Orks 0.0). The gate needs 1.0. The standard fixtures gave 0.0.
  • The 12 gate games had 0 SCRIPT ERROR lines.
  • Verdict: not_ready. FIX_SCREEN_VS_OBJECTIVE stays out of the AI. Nothing ships from the reserve track.

Stale bench and the fixture proposal

The V2-5 fixture proposal (commit 3ff20e3, 12:04 UTC) came from workflow wf_15c5f8f0-6ed: 6 agents, read-only, 0 games. A review that tried to disprove the proposal found 1 blocking issue, 5 major issues and 8 minor issues. Revision 2 answers that review.

Finding: the bench is stale

The 3 standard bench fixtures and the 3 reserve fixtures use rosters from 40kdc-data 1.0.19. The sweeps and the shipped game use 40kdc-data 1.4.5 with the 11th edition codex import.

Bench fixtures (40kdc-data 1.0.19)Sweeps and the shipped game (40kdc-data 1.4.5)
Custodescustodes_lions at 4dea059 (2026-10-17) or earlier: 11 units, 42 models, 2000 ptscustodes_lions: 9 units, 22 models, 1850 pts, 3 attachments
Orksrecon_stomps (Kult of Speed), old revision: 17 units, 77 models, 1975 ptsOrks_2000 (War Horde): 20 units, 106 models, 1975 pts, 5 attachments
Boardtake_and_hold_mirror_1 only29 official layouts

Units with the same name have different datasheets:

  • Allarus: on the bench, 5 models with M5 T7 W4 OC3. In the sweeps, 3 models with M7 T8 W6 OC2.
  • Gretchin: 11 models with OC2, against 10 models with OC1.
  • Stormboyz: 5 models, against 10.
  • Mek: Leader, against Support.

Result: the standard bench has the current datasheet for 0 of 44 clear and 0 of 42 harmful measured positions. Also, the current recon_stomps.json sums to 17 units, 75 models and 2280 pts, which is over 2000.

Proposal

Build asym_custodes_warhorde_2000_postdeploy first. P1 is the current custodes_lions (9 units, 22 models, 1850 pts). P2 is the current Orks_2000 (20 units, 106 models, 1975 pts). Do not build the Orks_2000 mirror or the Space Wolves mirror (the V2-5 draft) now.

  • Role. A separate extra gate. Do not pool its results with the standard fixtures. It has two jobs. (a) It can check that the V2-4 bundle also works, and does no harm, with other army lists. For that, its text (section 4.2) must be in a commit before the first game of that arm. The first AUD game started before this text was in a commit. Thus, for AUD, this fixture gives information only. (b) It is the required cross-faction no-harm check for each fix that acts on Orks_2000 units. Do not pool its results until a v3 rebuilds the stale standard fixtures.
  • Why this option. It has the current datasheet for 39 of 44 clear and 38 of 42 harmful positions. The Orks mirror has 16 of 44 and 25 of 42. The Space Wolves mirror has 5 of 44 and 4 of 42. It contains the matchup where the Lootas-to-centre options measured harmful (8 positions, 3 harmful, mean -1.82 VP). The rollout tool measured this matchup most: 177 jobs. The Custodes mirror had 153, and the Orks mirror had 118.
  • Cost (estimates). Engineering: 5.5 h or less. Validation: 1.0 to 1.6 container-hours for 24 games. Each 40-pair look: 3.3 to 5.3 container-hours. This adds 26% to 45% to a standard 124-pair look of 11.8 to 12.6 container-hours. A game takes 2.5 to 4 container-minutes, against 5 to 8 for an Orks mirror.
  • Limits. No fixture lets the Heavy branch of ranged_hold pass the gate. It gives at most 0.5 changed decisions per game on this option, and 0 on the Orks mirror. That needs a change to V2-1. No option has a confirmed finding with the datasheet, the context and a fix that can pass the gate.
  • Risks. 1850 against 1975 pts. The Orks always move second. A fix that acts only on Orks_2000 units acts in 1 game of 2 per pair. There are no attachments and no reserves. 420 Ork pts are Legends units. 40 pairs find only large harm (E below approximately -3.2 VP).

Status: the proposal waits for the decision of the owner. V2-5 says: propose, do not run.

Sources: tools/ai_lab/fixture_proposal.md (commit 3ff20e3, line 47 for the engineering cost), STATUS.md, 40k/armies/recon_stomps.json, Orks_2000.json and custodes_lions.json.

Tuning proposal (V2-6)

Round 5 closed at 08:57 UTC with a shipped gain of 0 VP. This is +0.5 VP or less. Thus V2-6 required a proposal for a parameter-tuning track. Workflow wf_a2eb71ab-c3d wrote it: 8 agents, read-only, 0 games. Two reviews revised it. Commit 5b00fe0 (09:30 UTC) holds it.

Recommendation: hold. Do no tuning before the V2-2 decision on the audit bundle. After that decision, run the one-generation probe one time at most. Do not run the drafted multi-stage track.

Probe design

8 candidates each move 8 parameters. Each move uses sd 0.3 times the default. The probe clips each value to the default times 1 plus or minus 0.5. A race gives each candidate 6 pairs (48 pairs). The top 4 get 12 more pairs (48 pairs). The pick is the best pooled E over 18 pairs (rule B). Then a V2-2 bench confirms it (stage C). An offline filter cut 273 parameters to 30. 86 of the 273 cannot act on these fixtures.

Cost (estimates)

ItemOne-generation probeDrafted multi-stage track
Engineering8.0 h (14 h or less if the lab builds T8 in full)–
Sibling sessions53 to 81251 to 279
Container-hours22.5 to 49.1 (expected 31 to 36)86 to 110
Wall time3.4 to 6.6 h on 14 containers (expected 4.4 to 5.1 h)10.3 to 13.5 h
LLM tokens$26 to $60 for the siblings, plus $13 to $20 or more for the parent (STATUS.md: approximately $39 to $80)–

The drafted track costs 3.6 times the container-hours of the probe at 1 look, and 2.3 times at 3 looks.

Odds (simulated)

Spread of true effects (tau)0.25 VP0.5 VP1.0 VP1.2 VP
P(ship and true gain above 0), probe0.0350.100.310.39
Added by the multi-stage track+0.004+0.015+0.086–

Simulation: rule B, sigma 10.26 VP per pair, 100,000 runs, mean true effect 0. In a near-null pool (a spread of 0.1 VP or less), the chance is 0.015 or less. In such a pool, most shipped candidates would have no real gain. V2-2 alone needs a true gain of 1.08 VP for a 50% chance, and 1.53 VP for 80%. The 5 measured code arms (pooled E -0.21 to +1.17) allow a spread up to approximately 1.2 VP.

Why hold

  • A shipped candidate would fit 3 bench fixtures with 0 attached leaders and 0 [HEAVY] weapons. 86 of 273 parameters cannot act on the bench fixtures. The bench Orks are Kult of Speed, not the Orks_2000 list of the sweeps.
  • The tuning tools have defects (found offline):
    • The tool cem_driver rates only the first candidate of each generation. Later candidates get n = 0.
    • The tuning tools never pass --rules11e. Thus they play legacy Take and Hold with the 10th edition deck. They use difficulty 2 by default. The bench uses difficulty 3.
    • The tools use --max-seconds 400, but 20.5% of 224 Custodes games ran longer.
    • When the ai_versions tag and the season collide, the tool reports the margins of the first candidate. It gives no warning. In a fake-godot test, candidate B played 0 games and reported the E of A (0.0). The true value was +6.0.
    • Rapid Ingress and Epic Challenge never set _current_player. The opponent of the unit decides From Golden Light (11.9 decisions per Custodes game).
    • AIPlayer.gd:1699 and :2788 call the AIDecisionMaker of HEAD directly. The tool determinism_check finds records by seed only.
  • Repair cost: 7.75 h to make the loop tools more reliable, and 9.0 h for the other fixes.

Sources: tools/ai_lab/tuning_track_proposal.md (commit 5b00fe0), STATUS.md.

Lessons

  1. Sweep rosters differ from bench rosters. The sweeps use the current Orks_2000 and custodes_lions lists. The bench uses Kult of Speed Orks and older Custodes data. The bench has the current datasheet for 0 of 44 clear and 0 of 42 harmful positions.
  2. At horizon 2, the re-check does not confirm most horizon-1 findings. At horizon 2, the re-check did not confirm 15 of 23 findings. The pr10 re-check confirmed 9 findings at horizon 1 with 24 seeds. Only 3 of them stayed confirmed at horizon 2. Two of them changed sign. One is s7475 round 2 (+4.00 to -3.00). The other is the s7463 round 1 corridor block (+4.79 to -1.63).
  3. The reach gate parks most critic-loop fixes. In round 5, no cluster got to a bench run (0 of 4). The charge_target fix had 0.33 changed declarations per game. The ranged_hold Heavy branch had 0. The marginal_oc and attack_move designs fired 0 to 1 times per game. On the reserve fixtures, the screen_vs_objective fix printed 0.17 lines per game. Most audit fixes passed (11 of 13), because their gate counts evaluation-level lines. The lab registered that less strict rule before the gate data.
  4. The bench has no attached leaders, no [HEAVY] weapons and almost no reserves. The bench has 0 leader attachments and 0 "heavy" strings. 84 of 84 units deploy at the start. But From Golden Light and On Gilded Wings put Allarus into reserves. This gives approximately 4 placements per game in the Custodes mirror.
  5. In a profile arm, a fix can also change the AI of the other seat. The opponent decides From Golden Light. Rapid Ingress and Epic Challenge never set _current_player. AIPlayer.gd:1699 and :2788 call the class directly. Before its repair, FIX_MOVE_TERRAIN_11E changed 175 of 361 opponent decisions. Bases from extracted copies avoid most of this.
  6. v1 shipped on small, uncertain gains. 1.56.7 shipped at +0.80 [-1.00, +2.60]. 1.56.8 shipped at +1.17 [-0.52, +2.86] (z approximately 1.36). V2-2 now needs z of 3.710 or more at look 1.
  7. Switch-off arms show the parts. RI alone gave nothing (-0.21). With LF on, it added +0.22.
  8. No simple rule separates over-charges from right charges. Over 77 positions, the sign of E depends on which mission gives VP for the result of the charge.
  9. Defects in the test tools can give wrong results. Examples:
    • the tag and season collision
    • a CEM driver that rates only the first candidate
    • legacy rules at difficulty 2
  10. Container restarts cost work. A container restart before 23:58 UTC on 30 October lost the scratchpad log and a workflow. The restart between 09:00 and 09:09 UTC stopped two workflows. Both resumed from their cache.

The AI on the branch plays as version 1.56.8 (commit e12e6e8). The 13 audit fixes are in the code (commit ca913e2), but every new parameter is at 0.0. With the parameters at 0.0, the AI plays as 1.56.8.

Commit 02acd70 (pushed) switched the round-2 fixes off again.

What the lab dropped or parked, and why

  • FIX_CHARGE_EV (round 1). The set without it (D) scored +1.58 VP per game against V6. The set with it (A) scored +0.97. Its own effect, from all round-1 bench data, was -0.75 VP [-2.48, +0.98]. The rule set before the data chose D.
  • FIX_FAR_TRIP (round 2). With FIX_OVERCOMMIT, it lost 6.26 VP per game in the Custodes mirror [-9.71, -2.81] (42 pairs). Pooled over the three fixtures, the result was -2.54 [-4.31, -0.77]. Units stayed back and scored less on cards that need units across the table.
  • FIX_OVERCOMMIT (round 2). Alone, it showed no gain. Custodes mirror: -1.62 (20 pairs). Asymmetric: -0.27 (15 pairs). Orks mirror: -8.25 (2 pairs, too few). Pooled: -3.38 [-5.48, -1.28].
  • FIX_KEEPER_RELEASE (round 3). All 124 bench pairs were identical (E 0.0). The bench showed no effect from the fix.
  • FIX_R1_SUPPORT_ADVANCE (round 4). V12 with it on scored -0.05 VP pooled. With it off, V12 scored +1.17. It is off in 1.56.8.
  • FIX_R1_HOME_CAPTURE (round 4). Parked. It fires 0 times on the 3 bench fixtures, because every home objective has a holder at deployment. It is off in V11, V12 and 1.56.8.
  • keeper_reach (round 4). Parked. It acts only inside the keeper release, which is off.
  • screen_vs_objective (round 4). Parked: the bench had no units in reserve at the start. On the 3 reserve fixtures, the final code printed 0.17 lines per game. The gate needs 1.0. It stays parked as a patch file.
  • charge_low_odds (round 4). No design won, and nothing merged. A round-5 study found no rule that separates over-charges from right charges.
  • Round 5. The marginal_oc panel had no winner. The attack_move cluster faded at horizon 2. The charge_target fix failed the fix gate (0.33 per game). For ranged_hold_vs_centre, the corridor branch faded at horizon 2. The Heavy branch has 0 bench reach.
  • Audit bundle. The fix gate parked FIX_CO_NEXT_PICK (0.83 lines per game) and FIX_SECURED_AWARE (0).
  • Shooting claims (rounds 1 and 2). None was measurable. In most cases, the AI already shot the claimed target, or the claim was about a weapon choice.

Code that is off stays in the AI, with its FIX_ parameter at 0. The round-5 designs and the screen_vs_objective final code stay as patch files in tools/ai_lab/. They are not in the AI.

Limits of this test

  • The bench uses old army lists (40kdc-data 1.0.19), with 0 attached leaders and 0 [HEAVY] weapons. The bench has the current datasheet for 0 of 44 clear and 0 of 42 harmful positions. Thus a bench gain possibly does not apply to the shipped game.
  • The Orks mirror is slow. The first round-1 bundle used a 900-second limit per game. Most Orks games against V0 did not finish. The round-1 re-test used 2400 seconds per game. Arm AUD uses 2400 seconds for the Orks mirror.
  • In the asymmetric fixture, one army wins almost every game. Thus win counts are not useful there. Use E.
  • In a profile arm, a fix can also change the AI of the other seat. The opponent decides From Golden Light. Rapid Ingress and Epic Challenge never set _current_player. AIPlayer.gd:1699 and :2788 call the AI class directly. A base without FIX_ parameters, or a base from an extracted copy, avoids most of this.
  • A horizon-1 rollout plays only to the end of the next battle round. Horizon 2 plays one more round. Neither plays the whole game, unless the decision is in round 4 or 5.
  • The rollout test could not measure the shooting claims. AI defenders never get the reactive shooting-stratagem window. Thus the bench cannot measure fixes for defensive stratagems.
  • The noise is large. In rounds 1 and 2, one pair of games had a standard deviation of approximately 12 to 13 VP. Four later code arms had 9.6 to 11.3 VP per pair. The 124-pair benches had a pooled SE of 0.39 to 0.92 VP.
  • In rounds 1 and 2, the primary and secondary columns count all finished games. This includes games whose pair did not finish. E uses complete pairs only.
  • Finished cloud sessions that are not archived can hold session slots. When too many exist, new sessions stay pending and do not start. Round 2 lost 3 sweep workers and 7 re-test shards to this. The lab stopped the last 8 round-2 bench shards before it read them.
  • Container restarts cost work. A container restart before 23:58 UTC on 30 October lost the scratchpad log and a workflow. The restart between 09:00 and 09:09 UTC on 31 October stopped two workflows. Both resumed from their cache.
